stories.title: Jensen Huang had a strict no one-on-one meetings rule for his 60 direct reports—and Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra: ‘We don’t waste a dime’
stories.summary: Nvidia’s ex-CEO Jensen Huang said frequent meetings cluttered his schedule—and interim CEO Colette Kress is just as obsessed with speed.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Jensen Huang had a strict no one-on-one meetings rule for his 60 direct reports—and Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra: ‘We don’t waste a dime’
sources.text: Former Nvidia CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang famously avoided unnecessary meetings, prioritizing efficiency over routine check-ins. Even with, at one point, 60 direct reports , he refused to do catch-ups. Now that he’s resigned , the question is whether his successor (currently Colette Kress who has stepped up on an interim basis) will keep the rule. Speaking at Stanford University , Huang once disclosed his aversion to frequent catch-ups. “I don’t do one-on-ones with any of them,” he said. Huang argued frequent meetings would clutter his schedule. He said they would also get in the way of the broader team’s ability to address challenges, work effectively, and stay transparent. “They never hear me say something to them, that is only for them to know,” he said. “There’s not one piece of information that I somehow secretly tell the staff; I don’t tell the rest of the company.” “In that way, our company was designed for agility. For information to be to flow as quickly as possible. For people to be empowered by what they are able to do, not what they know,” he added. But that doesn’t mean he had no time for his team. Huang insisted he still regularly caught up with his executives. They just didn’t need to set time aside in their diaries to be on the same page. “I write no reviews for any of them,” he added. “I give them constant reviews and they provide the same to me.” And when an employee genuinely needed a moment of his time, Huang insisted he’d “drop everything for them.” Stepping into Huang’s shoes (for now) is CFO Colette Kress . The interim CEO, who has an estimated net worth of $1.2 billion according to Forbes , holds a bachelor’s in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. After nearly three decades’ worth of financial roles at companies such as Texas Instruments , Cisco, and Microsoft , she joined Nvidia in September 2013. Since then, she guided the company’s finances through a significant transformation, from a business largely focused on video game hardware to a chipmaking powerhouse at the center of the AI boom—and watched its market cap soar from about $9 billion to, at its peak, $5 trillion. Its since dropped below $4 trillion upon the news regarding Huang. She hasn’t revealed whether she’ll ditch one-on-ones too. But the 59-year-old, who has spent 13 years as Huang’s right hand on Nvidia’s finances, seems to share his affinity for efficiency. “We do not waste a day, we don’t waste a dime,” Kress said in 2024. “And those two things are really important about us, our agility to move fast, but our ability to not waste things along the way.” Huang isn’t the first leader to argue that meetings aren’t the best use of time. Pandora’s former CEO Alexander Lacik told Fortune too many meetings result in every department or company issue getting “equal attention”—whether or not it needs it. He limited his catch-ups with management. “There’s only one, two, three activities that actually draw disproportionate value and the rest is just background noise,” he said. “As time has gone by and I’m getting towards the end of my career, I’m much more clear on trying to insert myself where I make a high impact.” United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby caps his meetings at four hours a day , and wants the ones he does attend to be “quick” and “almost all conversational.” E-commerce giant Shopify took one step further and actually axed all meetings involving more than two people in 2023, in a company-wide “calendar purge” meant to give employees more time to work on other tasks. And even Amazon founder Jeff Bezos—a big fan of “ messy meetings ”—mandates a strict protocol to ensure they’re actually useful, complete with a six-page memo instead of a PowerPoint (because they’re too vague) and half an hour set aside at the start of the meeting to silently read it together before having “a really elevated discussion.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on June 12, 2024.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
sources.text: Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too! In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China. Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role. However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top. More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway. The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are thinking he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations. All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering . It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day. And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal . Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well. Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday. Couple of really big outages out there: first, Microsoft Outlook , grounding a lot of office workers, then the whole damn U.S. air traffic control system , grounding thousands of flights. Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers. The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted. IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave wrote in his Special Breaking Analysis this week. Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn. Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, most of it not salacious, along with analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond: Breaking Analysis: Sovereign or not? Somebody give him back his Xanax! Also, I really don’t think mental illness is a compute problem. sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? Entenda aqui o que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang. /Com informações de Financial Times . sources.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
sources.text: The Steve Jobs of GPUs has been shown the door.﻿ On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium’s lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now. He has left Nvidia after seemingly enabling two chip smuggling scandals and allegedly having three extramarital affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy at the same time he was mingling with President Donald Trump. The world is watching to see if this scandal might disrupt the entire US AI industry and perhaps destabilize the stock market along with it. That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. And he didn’t plan for succession if he ever stepped down. The 63-year-old once said he preferred to die on the job ; he once suggested he’d work until he was 90 or 100 , then carry on leading the company as a robot. It’s not easy to replace Huang, partly because he had no deputies. Around 60 employees reported directly to the CEO . “He built the company around himself, and everything that happened there flowed through him,” says IDC analyst and former computing journalist Tom Mainelli. “Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen,” Jon Peddie, a computer industry analyst who’s been tracking Nvidia since its inception, tells me. But Nvidia isn’t Jensen anymore. He has left the company he cofounded 33 years ago. It’s the end of an era, and not just for Nvidia — because Jensen Huang was Big Tech’s last true example of a visionary showman founder CEO. “He was both the visionary and the tactical leader, the closest thing tech has had to Steve Jobs,” Moor Insights & Strategy chief analyst Pat Moorhead tells me. Elon Musk didn’t exactly found Tesla and has quite the track record of broken promises, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg has proven to be neither visionary nor showman so far. Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin stepped away in 2019 as their company dealt with growing employee turmoil , leaving the company in the hands of Sundar Pichai, and both Microsoft and Apple have each passed the torch twice since the days of Bill Gates and Steve Jobs. Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off. I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new. But even if Huang didn’t have the same gravitas as Jobs, he did have exciting tech up his sleeves and loved to demo it onstage. He knew how to get people excited about the future of visual computing with eye-opening gaming graphics, physics and lighting demos, and eventually image recognition, AI weather simulations, digital copies of real-world factories, and the robots that can virtually train in them. His Nvidia tried to educate people about the how and why of GPUs, too; I still remember in 2008 when Nvidia invited the Mythbusters to demo the difference between serial processing and parallel processing by firing a 1,100-nozzle paintball gun to “paint” the Mona Lisa in one shot. What I didn’t know back then: Huang was a visionary founder. He took Nvidia to fame and fortune through a series of tremendous bets. In 1996, three years after he cofounded the company at a Denny’s diner, Nvidia nearly went out of business while working on a failed graphics chip for the Sega Dreamcast game console. But even though he didn’t deliver that chip, Huang personally convinced Sega to invest $5 million afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024. He then turned around and bet the company again on the Riva 128 PC graphics accelerator, an effort so ambitious he had to lay off over half of Nvidia’s roughly 100 staffers, skip the prototyping stage, and rush it straight to production, and he still only had one month of payroll left by the time it shipped, The New Yorker wrote in 2023. Thankfully, it was a success, selling a million units in just four months and paving the way for both the GeForce GPU and a long-term relationship with chip fabricator TSMC. Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit , he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent. “Originally there was no market or market demand for it. It was almost as if they built it because they could,” says Peddie. “Jensen had the vision for what it could be and the courage to pursue it in spite of the opinions of others.” “NVIDIA was effectively investing in a computing platform that extended far beyond graphics,

sources.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. She previously was a financial journalist at Mergermarket covering M&A, private equity and venture capital. sources.text: Usually, we’d be offering to answer your questions about a news event, but honestly we don’t really have any answers about what the hell is going on over at Nvidia. I can’t speak for Nilay but at the rate Jensen Huang’s new mistresses are dropping, I am concerned we are approaching an affair Singularity . If things don’t decelerate soon, we may be looking at existential risk. Maybe the future of AI really does depend on Jensen’s sex life , but not in the way I was thinking ! As much fun (?) as we are having with all the assorted ladies, it’s important to stay focused on what’s really important : Chips and China. President Donald Trump was reportedly warned about Alice “No Relation” Huang’s possible connections to China’s spy apparatus last year, and again before his China trip in May. Nvidia reportedly intervened into a Commerce Department investigation into Alice’s company. Did Alice girlboss too close to the sun ? Have I been wrong all this time about AI being an important productivity tool, freeing everyone up to have multiple affairs at once? What do CEOs do at their jobs anyway? Is Jensen’s leather jacket really an alien symbiote ? Can’t I just go for a hike in peace ? Let’s discuss. Nilay and I will be joining you at 1PM ET.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia scandal draws in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agrees to testify about China chip sales
sources.text: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies. Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security. Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns." "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment. The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns." Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday. There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick. Criticism is mounting on President Donald Trump 's administration for declining to include over 100 companies highlighted as national security risks on a trade blacklist, including China's AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT, Reuters reported in June. Lutnick is a long-standing friend of Trump, with their relationship spanning over three decades, and is widely regarded as a close confidant of the President.

sources.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
sources.text: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. "Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick, Brandon Lutnick and Kyle Lutnick did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings. As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday. Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary. But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing . That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing , as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China . Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026 , with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings. Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China. "The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to nonpublic government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons. sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: Google lança modelo de IA veloz e eficiente; conheça o Gemini 4 Hydrogen
sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen , novo modelo de inteligência artificial desenvolvido para acelerar tarefas de programação e fluxos de trabalho executados por agentes de IA. Com foco em velocidade e eficiência, ele pode funcionar sozinho ou em conjunto com o Gemini 4 Carbon e o Gemini 4 Argon, modelos focados em atividades que exigem raciocínio mais complexo e de longo prazo. Segundo Koray Kavukcuoglu, vice-presidente sênior do Google DeepMind e arquiteto-chefe de IA do Google, o Hydrogen assume tarefas que precisam de execução rápida , e o Carbon e Argon cuidam das demandas mais complexas. No Google Antigravity, o recurso Orchestrator gerencia essa divisão e alterna entre os modelos durante uma mesma sessão. Em testes com o Terminal-Bench 4.0, o sistema alcançou resultados próximos aos do Carbon, com 24% menos consumo de cota e conclusão das tarefas 19% mais rápida. O Carbon também pode coordenar vários agentes Hydrogen, responsáveis pela execução e verificação de alterações em ambientes isolados. O Hydrogen oferece quatro níveis de raciocínio (low, medium, high e xhigh), que definem a quantidade de processamento dedicada a cada tarefa. No Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, marcou 51 pontos no nível high, acima dos 50 do Argon, e chegou a 54 pontos no xhigh. Na configuração padrão (high), é 2,5 vezes mais rápido que o Gemini 3.8 Flash. O desempenho em programação também melhorou: o modelo alcançou 57% de sucesso no Terminal-Bench 4.1, contra 18,2% da versão anterior, e reduziu em mais de cinco vezes a ocorrência de respostas com informações inventadas. Com janela de contexto de até 1 milhão de tokens de entrada e 1 milhão de tokens de saída , o modelo processa PDFs, planilhas, áudios e vídeos. Também extrai informações de arquivos enviados e serviços conectados, como Gmail, Google Drive, Airtable e Dropbox. No aplicativo Gemini, aciona ferramentas e habilidades adequadas com mais frequência e segue instruções de tom e formato ao longo de conversas com várias interações. O Google também destaca melhorias de segurança . Em comparação com o Gemini 3.8 Flash, o Hydrogen reduziu em até 81% as ações que ultrapassam as instruções recebidas e em até 79% as tarefas executadas abaixo do esperado. A ocorrência de ações desalinhadas com os objetivos caiu 12 vezes. Segundo o Google, 99,9% do processo de raciocínio do modelo é legível. Uma auditoria com mais de 200 mil interações também confirmou que não houve edições enganosas na cadeia de raciocínio . O Hydrogen ainda demonstrou ser mais de 2,3 vezes mais resistente a ataques de injeção indireta de comandos no benchmark Gray Swan IPI. No HealthBench Pro, menos de 0,4% das perguntas médicas e científicas receberam recusas indevidas. O lançamento também inclui mudanças na Busca do Google , disponível globalmente. A ferramenta ganha respostas mais visuais, aprimoramento de consultas para encontrar mais links relacionados e melhor interpretação de perguntas com várias partes, erros de digitação e solicitações específicas. No Google Sheets, o Gemini gera modelos financeiros interativos mais de 30% mais rápido que os modelos anteriores. Os resultados aparecem no canvas da ferramenta e se ajustam a diferentes cenários de previsão. O recurso está disponível a partir dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra, incluindo assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen está disponível no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca do Google . No plano gratuito, o aplicativo seleciona o modelo automaticamente, de acordo com a solicitação. Nos planos pagos, o modelo pode ser escolhido no seletor de modelos. Já a integração com o Google Sheets atende aos assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra. Já os desenvolvedores podem utilizar o modelo pela API Gemini, no Google AI Studio e no Android Studio . Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra também encontram a novidade no Google Antigravity. O preço da API é de US$ 1,50 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 por milhão de tokens de saída. No ambiente corporativo, o Hydrogen está disponível no Gemini para Empresas , tanto pela API quanto pelo seletor de modelos. A ferramenta também chegou ao Google Antigravity e ao Gemini para Google Sheets, neste último caso para assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 8 formas de assinar o Gemini mais barato ou de graça ”.

sources.title: Google lança Gemini 4 Hydrogen, IA intermediária e disponível para todos
sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen, novo grande modelo de linguagem (LLM) de nível intermediário. A inteligência artificial foi desenvolvida para entregar resultados com agilidade e eficiência, sendo indicada para tarefas cotidianas e fluxos de trabalho agênticos. O modelo está disponível em diferentes níveis de acesso ao Gemini , incluindo opções gratuitas e pagas. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen segue o padrão de nomenclatura baseado em elementos da tabela periódica , ao lado das IAs de fronteira Gemini 4 Carbon e Gemini 4 Argon . Porém, diferentemente dos demais, o Hydrogen não é uma variante de altíssima performance, mas uma opção pensada para atender a mais usuários e demandas em maior escala. Assim, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen é mais apropriado para tarefas cotidianas que não exigem raciocínio tão amplo ou elaborado quanto o oferecido pelos modelos mais avançados. Para complementar o lançamento, o Google apresentou o Orchestrator (“Orquestrador”, em português) dentro do Google Antigravity . A ferramenta alterna entre modelos como Carbon e Hydrogen durante uma mesma sessão, escolhendo a melhor opção conforme a complexidade da tarefa — o Carbon atua mais como coordenador, enquanto o Hydrogen é incorporado a agentes responsáveis por atividades mais objetivas. Segundo o Google, o Orchestrator alcançou uma taxa de sucesso próxima à do Gemini 4 Carbon no Terminal-Bench 4.0, mas consumiu 24% menos da cota de uso e concluiu as tarefas 19% mais rápido. Nos testes de benchmark, o Google comparou os resultados do Gemini 4 Hydrogen aos do Claude Sonnet 5.5 e do GPT-6.1 Terra , dois modelos de nível intermediário. Segundo os resultados apresentados pela empresa, a IA do Google supera os concorrentes na maioria dos testes, mas perde para o modelo da Anthropic nas avaliações de programação agêntica (Terminal-Bench 4.1), uso do computador (OSWorld-2.1) e matemática e ciências (Termina-Bench-Science 0.1). Segundo o Google, o novo modelo representa um salto significativo em inteligência e velocidade em relação ao Gemini 3.8 Flash , seu antecessor de nível intermediário. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen executa tarefas 2,5 vezes mais rápido em sua configuração de esforço alto e alcançou mais do que o triplo da pontuação no Terminal-Bench 4.1 (57% contra 18,2%), quando comparado ao modelo anterior. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen pode ser acessado em diferentes canais do ecossistema Google . Para desenvolvedores, o modelo está disponível na API Gemini, no Android Studio e no AI Studio. Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e AI Ultra também podem utilizá-lo no Google Antigravity. Quanto aos preços, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen cobra US$ 1,50 (R$ 8,46, em conversão direta) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 (R$ 42,29) por milhão de tokens de saída. Para usuários gratuitos e assinantes do Google AI Plus, o modelo pode ser acessado no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca. Vale lembrar que, a partir desta sexta-feira (13), os assinantes do plano AI Plus não poderão mais selecionar modelos da categoria Gemini Pro .
